headline: Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia is retaliating for Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centres while playing down damage to oil refineries.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: new today is Putin's first public acknowledgement of the data centre strikes, but it is a statement with no damage figures; remarks were made on 15 Oct 2026.
importance_line: The war now openly includes computing infrastructure on both sides, which puts AI work and the services that depend on it in Russia and Ukraine at risk, though the article gives no damage figures and Putin's remarks differ from his own Defense Ministry's reports.
summary: The Moscow Times reports that President Vladimir Putin said on 15 Oct 2026, by video link to the Delovaya Rossiya business association, 'They took the first step and we began to answer' over Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centres, his first public comments on the strikes on data centres run by Yandex and Sberbank this month, which our 15 Oct 2026 edition covered when Reuters reported that Ukrainian drones hit Sberbank's Balakovo data centre after three attacks on Yandex's. The paper notes that his remarks contradict the Russian Defense Ministry's own reports that it began striking Ukrainian data centres last month, and that Putin brushed off refinery attacks, including a fire at Rosneft's Ryazan refinery, as 'nothing particularly significant'.
notes: Read in full. Follow-up of the Sberbank data centre story in the 15 Oct 2026 edition (item 4, Reuters) and its pool entry of The Moscow Times. The 15 Oct 2026 edition filed that story under Politics and government; default category here is ENE, so the main session may move it to POL. Putin's remarks were on Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
